g.text: Second Renaissance: a theory of change people can argue with
Co-initiate a Second Renaissance: a conscious transformation of foundational views, values, practices, and
institutions toward a wiser, weller, regenerative civilization.
The first prerequisite since June is still open: decide together how the trees change. Who will
steward a time-boxed review of the goal, the main problems and the constraint hypothesis, and
Hold the stewarded review: invite the people the trees affect, circulate the model
first, agree what 'good enough for provisional use' means, and keep minority
The 2R research circle (steward to be named)
Facilitate one bounded stewarded review of the goal, priority UDEs, and
A dated model records confirmed, disputed and still-provisional items, the
evidence for each, a named steward, a decision rule and the next review date
The review runs past its time box, or disagreement is being smoothed over to reach
Every later step (a throughput definition, an entry path, recurring practice)
assumes trees the group has accepted. The count shows no change to the trees from
late July through August, and nothing merges into them yet: the first prerequisite
from June, deciding together how the trees change, is still open.
How it got here: 24 steps by 4 people, from 5 Jun 2026 to 4 Sep 2026. This is the Second
Renaissance's shared reasoning: a movement's strategy written as trees, then argued with,
reorganised and partly rebuilt by the people working on it. Step back through how it got here, or
look at the one action it says comes next. Quoted words are real and dated from their sources.
Tree changes are an editor's reading of what each step changed. Dates marked ≈ are approximate.
Italic narration is the editor's. ◀ Earlier steps back; History lists every step; Ctrl+T shows
the trees as they stand now.
